title: ST0025's AT01 and AT02 go green on the regression they name: they prove ink exists, not that the stamp was made for the page
body:
ST0025-AT01 asserts that every page of a mixed-geometry output carries ink in its centre band, and AT02 that no page carries ink in its margin strips. Both pass on the DEFECT they exist to prevent.

MEASURED BY cc on 2026-09-22, first-hand rather than by reading: it built the three-page fixture with stampz's own `_emit_fixture`, rendered ONE A4 stamp with `_render_stamp`, laid it over all three pages with `qpdf --overlay --repeat=1` -- which is exactly the old behaviour ST0025 replaced -- and ran the two assertions' own arithmetic against the result. AT01's centre band reads 1237, 1289 and 1237, all greater than zero, so it passes on every page. AT02's 5% margin strips read 0, 0 and 0, so it passes on every page.

WHY THEY WENT RED BEFORE THE FIX, and why that was not a regression guard: the old code REFUSED a mixed-geometry file, so `assert_success` failed. That is a one-time red against a refusal, not a check that can distinguish a stamp made for the page from one made for another page. AC02's own sentence claims the discriminating power it does not have: "which is what tells a stamp made for the page from one made for another page and drawn wherever it lands." That sentence is false as measured, and it is the same class as the `AT13: PASS` postcondition deleted from `hoist-rebase.sh` this morning under issue 0049: a check that cannot go red.

WHAT THE DISCRIMINATOR HAS TO KEY ON: the mark's size scaling with the page. vc's own numbers are the signal -- a stamp made for the page gives 1314, 4638 and 1314 bytes of ink on A4, wide and A4, where one A4 stamp over all three gives 1157 on the wide page, LESS than the A4 pages take. Two candidate forms, both threshold-light: the wide page's centre-band ink must EXCEED each A4 page's (4638 > 1314 correct, 1157 < 1314 regression), or the ink's horizontal bounding box on each page must span most of that page's own width (about 80% correct, 41% on the wide page under the regression, because the mark is an A4 mark). cc tried a third form, ink in the outer part of the wide page's own centre band, and MEASURED IT NOT WORKING: 274 correct against 252 regressed.

NOT A DEFECT IN BEHAVIOUR: stampz itself is correct and proven by the by-hand runs recorded on ST0025 and in 63661de. What is wrong is the strength of the guard left behind, which is the thing that would let the behaviour regress unnoticed.
